# Independent review of the actual seven Clippy substitutions

No blocking defect found in the exact authored root and locals patches. This review read the retained complete before/after sources, actual patches, maps, the failed Clippy stderr and surrounding current consumers. It verified archived identities and the locals unified diff. The selected-input map records the exact inputs and separately observed current sources; subsequent root formatting is a separate recorded operation.

The four locals changes replace `checked_add(addend).unwrap_or(usize::MAX)` with `saturating_add(addend)`. Both produce the same usize for every representable value and overflow. The same child addends, task branches and traversal order remain; each block statement still charges its original span before adding its child count. The distinct chained runtime-call sum and all lexical identities, scope restoration and other accounting branches are unchanged.

The three selected replacements split lazy `filter_map(predicate.then(|| payload))` into lazy `filter(predicate).map(payload)`. Both inspect each formal in original order and evaluate the same clone/index payload only for matching Natural, Basis or Operation categories. Nonmatching formals never perform an index lookup or clone. The same collection types and already located checks/payments remain. There is no eager clone, extra profile allowance, changed provider condition, or moved error priority.

I authored earlier finite consumption, lexical helper and concrete runtime-group changes, but did not author these root/A Clippy substitutions. This is an independent review of those warning repairs, not an independent review of my earlier work. No build, test, CLI, native capture, formatter, metadata refresh or active inventory write was performed by this review. The original attempt-08 Clippy failure remains a failure; a future successful validation cannot be inferred from static equivalence. The edits create no constitutional adoption, guarantee discharge, source preservation or Issue completion claim.
